justification: Critical: /api/property served a different property's zone, controls and DCP rules for an address the user typed (DQ-122, P1), with nothing on screen saying so. Every downstream panel on the assessment page and the precinct lookup inherit the lot this function picks.

pre_impl.existing_data: No database table involved: the lot comes from the NSW Planning Portal address search (ePlanningApi/address), checked against the NSW address register (NSW_Geocoded_Addressing_Theme AddressPoint) with 893 New South Head Road as a positive control.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The code assumed the Portal's top-ranked candidate is the asked address. The Portal search is fuzzy: for 700 New South Head Rd Rose Bay it returns ten candidates, none numbered 700, and the scorer ignored every token starting with a digit so the house number was never compared.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No house-number parser existed in frontend-nextjs (grep houseNumber, streetNumber, parseHouse, numberMatch). The new helper lib/address-number-match.ts is used by searchProperty and its valuation fallback; nothing parallel was built.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A Portal 429 rate limit, timeout or non-list body previously became null and then read as Property not found. It now throws Address search unavailable, which reaches the user as a service error (500), never as a 404 not-found.
pre_impl.frontend_type: API returns 404 with JSON {success:false, error:string, notFound:true}. usePropertyAssessment now reads body.error on a non-OK response, so the page prints that string instead of HTTP 404: Not Found.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a neighbouring lot's controls shown silently under the typed address. After: a red message naming the address that was not found; a real address the matcher rejects would show the same visible message, never another property.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Against production (old code) it exits 1: 700 returns 893, 235 returns 582, 14 Hunter St returns 8-12 Hunter St. It also fails if a fix refuses the three real control addresses.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Production run 2026-10-04: DQ-122: 3 of 6 addresses answered wrongly (893, 582, 14 8-12 HUNTER STREET). Local fixed build: exit 0, every address returned itself or said not found.

functions.name: filterToAskedProperty
functions.input: asked address string and the Portal candidate list
functions.output: only candidates with matching street number or containing range, street name and type, and postcode
functions.if_none: empty list, which searchProperty turns into null and the route into a 404 naming the address

functions.name: NSWPlanningPortalService.searchProperty
functions.input: the address string the user typed or chose from Google Places
functions.output: the matching Portal candidate, or null when none matches
functions.if_none: null; a failed request throws Address search unavailable instead of returning null

break_it.scenario: Same number, different street: 14 Hunter St Lewisham where the Portal's top hit is 14 ST JOHN STREET LEWISHAM
break_it.what_happens: Number-only matching would serve the St John Street lot under a Hunter Street address
break_it.how: streetMatches compares street name words and type
break_it.repro: jest: same number on a different street is a different property; mutation removing the street check fails 2 tests

break_it.scenario: Same number and street in another suburb or postcode, e.g. 12 Smith St Summer Hill vs Ashfield
break_it.what_happens: Street and number matching alone would serve the Ashfield lot for a Summer Hill address
break_it.how: postcode must equal when both sides carry one
break_it.repro: jest: same number and street in another postcode; mutation removing the postcode check fails 1 test

break_it.scenario: Portal rate-limits (429) or returns a non-list body during a lookup
break_it.what_happens: Previously read as Property not found; with the new 404 would tell the user the address does not exist
break_it.how: searchProperty throws Address search unavailable and getPropertyComplianceData rethrows it, so it surfaces as a 500 service error
break_it.repro: jest: a rate limit is an outage; mutation returning null fails 2 tests

break_it.scenario: Real addresses written with level or unit designators (L1 32 PHILLIP STREET) or ranges (674-680)
break_it.what_happens: An over-strict matcher would refuse real properties and show not found wrongly
break_it.how: unit words and letter-digit designators are skipped; a number inside a range matches
break_it.repro: Measured 101 of 101 real register addresses across 14 suburbs resolve to themselves; the one miss found (L1) was fixed and pinned by a jest case

break_it.scenario: A fix that answers not found for every address would turn DQ-122 green
break_it.what_happens: The check would pass while the lookup is broken
break_it.how: probe requires the three register-held controls to come back as themselves
break_it.repro: pytest test_dq122_red_when_a_real_address_is_refused; mutation accepting not_found for real addresses fails it

break_it.scenario: Valuation fallback walks candidates when the first has no valuation (strata)
break_it.what_happens: The fallback would pick any neighbouring lot that happens to have valuation data
break_it.how: fallback candidates pass through the same filterToAskedProperty

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes -- after Vercel deploys, run python scripts/dq_probe_app_defects.py --id DQ-122 against production; on exit 0 flip DQ-122 to fixed in dq_checks.json and the tracker in a follow-up.
